To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extent to and the way in which people suffer from overload are closely related to their strategies to cope with it.

information overload is related to the coping strategies people use to manage information, that people who suffer most from information overload are those who use the most coping strategies, and that the coping strategies people choose are influenced by their personal characteristics and by the information environment.
information overload is a serious problem for many senior managers and that the extent to and the ways in which people cope with it are related to their personality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people cope with information overload and how this coping process influences the extent to which they suffer from overload.
the question of why some people seem more affected by information overload than others.
information overload as a problem of coping with information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
people who suffer from information overload are not those who are overloaded, but those who do not know how to cope with the information overload.

people with a strong preference for a particular information processing strategy (analytical, holistic or social) are more likely to experience information overload than people who are flexible and can adapt their strategy to the situation.
the extent to information overload is a function of the strategies people use to cope with it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
information overload is not an inherent characteristic of a person but a consequence of the strategies that person uses to cope with the information environment.

people with a proactive approach, that is, those who are able to control their information processing, are less prone to suffer from information overload than those who are reactive and who let information processing control them.
information overload is not a matter of the quantity of information but rather a matter of the way it is used.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extent of the problem of information overload is not necessarily the main issue.
people who suffer most from information overload are the ones who do not have a clear sense of their information needs and do not know how to prioritize information.
the strategies people use to cope with information overload depend on their personality and on their work context.
